answer: A bond paid in incompressible work makes each identity cost real compute: an agent must hash its public key into a spiral of nonces until the digest meets the epoch target, and peers settle only with work that is unique. Cloning a thousand agents thus needs a thousand separate mining runs, while copied chains are rejected on-ledger. Emissions split by distinct work, not headcount, so a swarm earns no more than one honest agent yet spends far more energy, and a seeded prism assigns queue slots that near-identical sonnet bundles cannot cheaply fill.
